artifacts.notes: Complete transcription of the whole book, 1,149,343 bytes, front matter through the end, including the full table of contents and chapter LI. Exact acquired bytes: lines 1-26 and everything from the 'END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK' line at 18756 onward are Project Gutenberg header, licence and trademark matter and are not Twain's text, so a raw literal search over this artifact can match Project Gutenberg's own prose as well as the book's.
artifacts.rights_basis: The Innocents Abroad was published in 1869 and Samuel Clemens died in 1910, so the text is in the public domain in the United States and in life-plus-70 jurisdictions. Project Gutenberg states in the file itself that the eBook 'is for the use of anyone anywhere in the United States and most other parts of the world at no cost and with almost no restrictions whatsoever', to be copied, given away or re-used under the Project Gutenberg License included with it. The exact bytes are retained here with that header, licence and trademark notice intact, so the file is redistributed on the terms Project Gutenberg attaches to it.

work.author: Mark Twain
work.description: Mark Twain's narrative of the 1867 Quaker City excursion to Europe and the Holy Land. Chapter LI reaches the gate of Nain and sets down Luke 7:12-16 entire - the appointed Gospel of the Fifteenth Sunday after Pentecost - and then, in the next paragraph, has the pilgrims breaking souvenirs off the mosque wall while standing on the praying carpets. A locus is a chapter.
work.title: The Innocents Abroad, or The New Pilgrims' Progress
